intro: Regulatory affairs is present at every stage of a medicine's life. We shape the development plan and regulatory strategy before the first study, build the CMC, non-clinical and clinical evidence into the dossier, steer the application through authority review towards approval, and then keep the authorisation current through every variation, renewal and change.
coverIntro: End-to-end regulatory strategy for biologics, biosimilars and small molecules, from development through approval and beyond.

services.title: Development & CMC strategy
items: Regulatory design and review of comparative studies: analytical and functional biosimilarity exercises for biologics; pharmaceutical equivalence and bioequivalence programmes for small molecules
Regulatory oversight of CMC development, from cell-bank characterisation or drug-substance route selection, through specification setting and stability, to process validation and technology transfer
Comparability and change-control protocols for process, site and scale changes, for both biological and synthetic products

services.title: Dossier authoring & readiness
items: CTD technical authoring and review, Modules 1–4; eCTD preparation
Regulatory and quality gap analysis prior to filing
Pre-assessment review of dossiers from the assessor's perspective

services.title: Agency interaction & intelligence
items: Scientific advice and pre-submission meeting strategy, briefing documents and preparation (EMA, MHRA, national agencies)
Structured responses to agency questions and deficiency letters
Local requirement mapping and regional regulatory intelligence

services.title: Post-approval & lifecycle
items: Variations, amendments and renewals across regions
Post-approval commitments and their follow-up with agencies
Regulatory assessment of post-approval process, site and supplier changes

services.title: GMP & quality compliance
services.kicker: EU GMP · PIC/S · WHO GMP · ICH Q7–Q12
items: GMP gap assessment of manufacturing and testing sites against EU GMP (including Annex 1 and Annex 2), PIC/S and WHO requirements
Inspection readiness: mock inspections, pre-approval inspection preparation and front-room / back-room coaching
Response to inspection findings: root-cause analysis, CAPA plans and follow-up evidence packages for the agency
Site Master File, GMP certificate and manufacturing-authorisation applications; QP declarations for imported products
Pharmaceutical quality system design and review: change control, deviations, OOS, complaints and product quality review
Data integrity assessment
Supplier and CMO qualification: audits, quality and technical agreements, and ongoing oversight
Alignment of GMP documentation with the dossier: validation, stability and batch records that say the same thing the CTD says

fileIntro: Select an authority to see the submission routes we handle there. Authorities are grouped the way the industry ranks them: WHO-Listed Authorities and long-standing ICH regulators first, then other ICH members and observers, regional procedures and national reliance routes.

authorities.name: European Medicines Agency
authorities.footnote: All EU procedures, including EDQM CEP and ASMF for active substances.

procedures.name: Centralised Procedure (CP)
procedures.note: Single application assessed by CHMP; mandatory for biotech-derived products and biosimilars. One authorisation valid in all EU/EEA states.

procedures.name: Decentralised Procedure (DCP)
procedures.note: Simultaneous application in several member states with a Reference Member State; the usual route for generics.

procedures.name: Mutual Recognition Procedure (MRP)
procedures.note: Extension of an existing national authorisation to further member states.

procedures.name: National procedure
procedures.note: Single-country authorisation where the product is not intended for other EU markets.

procedures.name: Scientific advice & pre-submission
procedures.note: CHMP/SAWP scientific advice, pre-submission meetings and eligibility requests before filing.

procedures.name: CEP and ASMF (EDQM)
procedures.note: Certificate of Suitability or Active Substance Master File so the API can be referenced in any EU dossier.

authorities.name: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
authorities.footnote: CDER and CBER routes; Type II DMFs for active substances.

procedures.name: NDA — 505(b)(1)
procedures.note: Full new drug application with complete safety and efficacy data.

procedures.name: NDA — 505(b)(2)
procedures.note: Relies in part on published data or a listed drug; the route for reformulations and new indications.

procedures.name: ANDA — 505(j)
procedures.note: Abbreviated application for generics, demonstrating bioequivalence to the reference listed drug.

procedures.name: BLA — 351(a) and 351(k)
procedures.note: Biologics License Application (the FDA's formal name); 351(k) is the biosimilar and interchangeable pathway.

procedures.name: Pre-IND / Type B–C meetings
procedures.note: Formal meeting requests, briefing packages and written responses.

procedures.name: Drug Master File (Type II)
procedures.note: Confidential API, intermediate or packaging information referenced by the applicant.

authorities.name: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
authorities.footnote: Post-Brexit routes for Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

procedures.name: National marketing authorisation
procedures.note: Full UK assessment under the 150-day national procedure.

procedures.name: International Recognition Procedure (IRP)
procedures.note: Reliance on an approval from a Reference Regulator (EMA, FDA, Swissmedic, Health Canada, TGA and others); Route A or B.

procedures.name: Scientific advice
procedures.note: MHRA scientific advice meetings and written advice before submission.

procedures.name: Variations and renewals
procedures.note: Type IA/IB/II variations and renewals aligned to the EU framework.

authorities.name: Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products
authorities.footnote: Standard, fast-track and foreign-approval-based procedures.

procedures.name: Standard authorisation
procedures.note: Full assessment of a new active substance or a known active substance.

procedures.name: Procedure with prior foreign approval (Art. 13 TPA)
procedures.note: Reduced assessment relying on an authorisation from a comparable foreign authority.

procedures.name: Fast-track and temporary authorisation
procedures.note: Accelerated routes for medicines meeting an urgent medical need.

procedures.name: Pre-submission meeting
procedures.note: Scientific and procedural advice before filing.

authorities.name: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency
authorities.footnote: PMDA review, MHLW approval; Japanese-language Module 1 and 2.

procedures.name: New drug application (J-NDA)
procedures.note: Full application including Japanese bridging or local clinical data where required.

procedures.name: Biosimilar application
procedures.note: Comparability-based application under the Japanese biosimilar guideline.

procedures.name: Generic application
procedures.note: Bioequivalence-based application with Japanese specification requirements.

procedures.name: PMDA consultation
procedures.note: Formal clinical and quality consultations before submission.

authorities.name: Health Canada
authorities.footnote: Common Electronic Submissions Gateway; bilingual labelling.

procedures.name: New Drug Submission (NDS)
procedures.note: Full submission for a new active substance or new indication.

procedures.name: Abbreviated New Drug Submission (ANDS)
procedures.note: Generic submission demonstrating bioequivalence to the Canadian reference product.

procedures.name: Biosimilar NDS
procedures.note: Comparability-based submission under the Canadian biosimilar guidance.

procedures.name: Drug Master File
procedures.note: API and other master files referenced in the submission.

authorities.name: Therapeutic Goods Administration
authorities.footnote: Registration on the ARTG; comparable-overseas-regulator reliance.

procedures.name: Category 1 registration
procedures.note: Full evaluation of a new prescription medicine.

procedures.name: COR-A / COR-B reliance pathways
procedures.note: Abbreviated evaluation relying on an unredacted assessment report from a comparable overseas regulator.

procedures.name: Generic registration
procedures.note: Bioequivalence-based application against the Australian reference product.

procedures.name: Pre-submission planning form
procedures.note: Mandatory pre-submission step defining the dossier and timetable.

authorities.name: Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária
authorities.footnote: Portuguese-language dossier; GMP certification of all sites is a prerequisite.

procedures.name: New medicine registration
procedures.note: Full registration of a new synthetic molecule or a new fixed-dose combination.

procedures.name: Generic and similar medicines
procedures.note: Bioequivalence and pharmaceutical equivalence against the Brazilian comparator.

procedures.name: Biological products
procedures.note: Comparability (biosimilar) or individual development pathway.

procedures.name: Optimised analysis (reliance)
procedures.note: Reduced assessment for products approved by an Equivalent Foreign Regulatory Authority.

procedures.name: Post-registration changes
procedures.note: Variations and renewals under the ANVISA change categories.

authorities.name: National Medical Products Administration
authorities.footnote: Chinese-language dossier; CDE technical review.

procedures.name: Imported drug registration (Class 5)
procedures.note: Registration of a product already approved abroad, with Chinese clinical data where required.

procedures.name: New drug application (Class 1–2)
procedures.note: Innovative or improved new drugs under the 2020 Drug Registration Regulation.

procedures.name: Biosimilar application
procedures.note: Comparability-based application under NMPA biosimilar guidance.

procedures.name: API / excipient / packaging platform filing
procedures.note: DMF-type registration on the CDE platform, linked to the drug application.

procedures.name: Pre-submission communication
procedures.note: CDE consultation meetings before filing.

authorities.name: Türkiye İlaç ve Tıbbi Cihaz Kurumu
authorities.footnote: EU-aligned framework; on-site GMP inspection before authorisation.

procedures.name: Marketing authorisation application
procedures.note: National application in CTD/eCTD format under the EU-aligned regulation.

procedures.name: Biosimilar application
procedures.note: Comparability-based application under the Turkish biosimilar guideline.

procedures.name: GMP certificate application
procedures.note: Inspection of foreign manufacturing sites as a prerequisite to authorisation.

procedures.name: Variations and renewals
procedures.note: Type IA/IB/II variations mirroring the EU classification.

authorities.name: Saudi Food and Drug Authority
authorities.footnote: National route alongside the GCC centralised procedure.

procedures.name: New drug registration
procedures.note: Full national application for a new active substance.

procedures.name: Generic and biosimilar registration
procedures.note: Bioequivalence or comparability-based applications.

procedures.name: Verification and abridged pathways
procedures.note: Reduced review for products approved by a reference authority.

procedures.name: Site registration and GMP
procedures.note: Registration of the manufacturing site and GMP clearance before filing.

authorities.name: Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios
authorities.footnote: Spanish-language dossier; equivalence agreements with reference regulators.

procedures.name: New molecule registration
procedures.note: Full registration after the New Molecule Committee opinion.

procedures.name: Generic registration
procedures.note: Bioequivalence-based registration against the Mexican reference product.

procedures.name: Biotechnological and biocomparable products
procedures.note: Comparability-based application for biosimilars.

procedures.name: Equivalence-agreement reliance
procedures.note: Expedited review for products approved by FDA, EMA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, TGA and others.

authorities.name: Egyptian Drug Authority
authorities.footnote: WHO maturity level 3 authority.

procedures.name: Marketing authorisation
procedures.note: National registration in CTD format.

procedures.name: Biosimilar registration
procedures.note: Comparability-based application under EDA biosimilar guidelines.

procedures.name: Reliance pathway
procedures.note: Abridged review for products approved by a stringent authority.

procedures.name: Variations and re-registration
procedures.note: Post-approval changes and periodic re-registration.

authorities.name: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority
authorities.footnote: Reliance and collaborative review routes.

procedures.name: New registration application
procedures.note: Full national assessment in eCTD format.

procedures.name: Reliance (abridged) review
procedures.note: Reduced assessment for products approved by a recognised regulatory authority.

procedures.name: Biosimilar application
procedures.note: Comparability-based application under SAHPRA biosimilar guidance.

procedures.name: Amendments and renewals
procedures.note: Post-registration changes and periodic renewals.

authorities.name: GCC Centralised Registration
authorities.region: Saudi Arabia · UAE · Kuwait · Qatar · Oman · Bahrain
authorities.footnote: GCC-DR centralised procedure with national filings alongside.

procedures.name: Centralised registration (GCC-DR)
procedures.note: Single application assessed for all member states, followed by national pricing and listing.

procedures.name: National registration
procedures.note: Direct filings with each national authority where the centralised route is not used.

procedures.name: Site registration and GMP
procedures.note: Registration of manufacturing sites, including GCC GMP inspections.

procedures.name: CPP and legalisation
procedures.note: Certificates of Pharmaceutical Product and document legalisation requirements.

authorities.name: EAEU Unified Registration
authorities.footnote: Common rules of the Eurasian Economic Union.

procedures.name: Mutual recognition procedure
procedures.note: Assessment by a Reference State, recognised by the chosen Recognition States.

procedures.name: Decentralised procedure
procedures.note: Simultaneous assessment by several member states.

procedures.name: Bringing national registrations into line
procedures.note: Transition of legacy national dossiers to the Union format.

procedures.name: GMP inspection (EAEU)
procedures.note: Union GMP certificate as a prerequisite for registration.

authorities.name: Latin America — national authorities
authorities.footnote: Spanish-language dossiers; CPP and GMP certification required.

procedures.name: National registration
procedures.note: Full application with each national authority.

procedures.name: Reliance and abridged review
procedures.note: Reduced assessment relying on a stringent-authority approval and public assessment report.

procedures.name: Renewals and variations
procedures.note: Country-specific post-approval change categories.

authorities.name: Middle East and North Africa — national authorities
authorities.footnote: Including Iran’s IRC registration and emergency-import routes.

procedures.name: IFDA registration (IRC)
procedures.note: Iranian registration via the IRC, including import licensing and pricing.

procedures.name: Emergency and unlicensed import
procedures.note: Case-by-case import authorisation for urgently needed medicines.

procedures.name: National registration
procedures.note: Direct filings with Iraqi, Jordanian and Lebanese authorities.

procedures.name: Variations and renewals
procedures.note: Post-approval changes under each national framework.

authorities.name: CIS — national authorities outside the EAEU
authorities.footnote: Russian-language dossiers and local reference requirements.

procedures.name: National registration
procedures.note: Full application under each national regulation.

procedures.name: Accelerated registration
procedures.note: Reduced review for products approved by a stringent authority.

procedures.name: Re-registration
procedures.note: Periodic renewal of national authorisations.

authorities.name: Africa — national and collaborative routes
authorities.footnote: National and collaborative (ZaZiBoNa, AMA) assessment routes.

procedures.name: National registration
procedures.note: Full application with each national authority.

procedures.name: Collaborative and joint assessment
procedures.note: Work-sharing procedures such as ZaZiBoNa and African Medicines Agency initiatives.

procedures.name: Reliance on WHO prequalification or SRA approval
procedures.note: Abridged review for prequalified or stringent-authority-approved products.

intelligence.intro: A dossier is only as good as the guidance it was written against. We track what the agencies change, and we use AI tools, under qualified human review, to turn that information into faster, more consistent regulatory work.

groups.title: Regulatory intelligence
items: Continuous monitoring of EMA, FDA, MHRA, WHO, PMDA, TGA and ICH guideline publications, concept papers and public consultations, with a focus on biologics, biosimilars and GMP
Impact assessment of each change on your pipeline and marketed products, with a recommended action and deadline
Country requirement mapping and regulatory landscape reports for market-entry decisions
Precedent analysis: EPARs, assessment reports, approval histories and public agency correspondence on comparable products
Periodic intelligence briefings tailored to your portfolio and target regions

groups.title: AI in regulatory work
items: AI-assisted screening of dossiers against current guidelines and agency expectations before filing: a faster first pass that our assessors then verify
Automated consistency checks across CTD modules: specifications, batch data, stability claims and cross-references
Structured first drafts of responses to agency questions, built from your source data and finalised by a regulatory professional
Advice on using AI in GxP-regulated work: validation expectations, data-integrity safeguards and documentation in line with emerging EMA and FDA guidance
Regulatory data standardisation: IDMP/SPOR-ready product data and eCTD-compliant publishing

intelligence.principle: AI accelerates review and drafting. It never decides. Every regulatory decision and every page that reaches an agency is owned, reviewed and signed off by a qualified regulatory professional.
